LESSON: PLAYING STRING MUSICAL INSTRUMENTS

Grade: SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade three
Subject: CREATIVE ACTIVITIES
Strand: Performing and Display
Topic 2.5: Playing String Musical Instruments
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 14

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Playing String Musical Instruments, part of Performing and Display in SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade three CREATIVE ACTIVITIES.

Key inquiry question: How are string instruments played? 2. Which materials are used for improvising a musical string instrument?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Playing String Musical Instruments together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Communication and collaboration: The learner visually and aurally identities and talks about the string instruments from

the recordings and pictures.

• Creativity and imagination: The learner uses locally available materials to improvise a string instrument.

• Self- efficacy: The learner confidently plays the improvised string instrument.

Values:
• Responsibility: The learner takes care of digital devices as they record and play string musical instruments for enjoyment.

• Unity: The learner cooperates with others as they work in pairs to identify and talk about the string instruments from the

recordings and pictures.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
• Environmental conservation: The learner responsibly uses locally available materials to improvise string instruments

• Self-awareness and self-esteem: The learner plays the string instrument for enjoyment.

Link to other subjects:

Environmental activities: The learner identifies string instruments from different Kenyan communities.

Suggested learning resources

Open space, reusable locally available material for making improvised fiddle, musical bows and mouth bows, resource

persons, visual recordings of musical instrument, flash cards, digital devices with assistive technologies for the hearing
